requirements.statement: Each label given to a form field through aria-label, where it provides the field's label, lets the user know the exact function of that field.

citations.quote: Chaque étiquette implémentée via l’attribut WAI-ARIA `aria-label` permet-elle de connaître la fonction exacte du champ de formulaire auquel elle est associée ?
Retrouver dans le document les champs de formulaire dont l’étiquette est fournie par un attribut WAI-ARIA `aria-label`

routes.statement: The content of the aria-label attribute is relevant: it lets the user know the nature, type or format of the information the field expects.

citations.quote: Pour chaque champ de formulaire, vérifier que le contenu de l’attribut est pertinent
Texte à proximité du champ de formulaire permettant d’en connaître la nature, le type ou le format des informations attendues.

exceptions.statement: When the field also has aria-labelledby, the glossary's order of the accessible name makes the referenced passage the field's label, and the aria-label is not the one evaluated for relevance.

citations.quote: Cet ordre doit être utilisé pour l’évaluation de la pertinence de l’étiquette

rationale.text: Relevance is judgment, so the entry is not full. The candidate is none, by decision Q48. The custom check looks at a native field whose only label mechanism is an aria-label attribute with empty content: rendered, exposed and visible, with an aria-label that is empty or only ASCII whitespace, no aria-labelledby, no associated <label>, no title and no placeholder. It abstains on every other case, including every non-empty aria-label, whose relevance is judgment. Its fault is evidence only. The wording asks about each label implemented by an aria-label attribute, and the methodology selects fields whose label is provided by one. An empty aria-label is present, but it does not give the field its label: browsers skip an empty aria-label when they compute the name, and the glossary judges relevance on the source that actually labels the field. So this test may not apply to such a field at all: on that reading the field has no label, which is a fault under test 11.1.1, not under this one. Fabien chose to demote rather than rule (Q48). The link keeps its routes and its whole scope and becomes evidence_only; the check never answers no_fault, so its scope supports no positive result. What would raise the entry: a ruling that an empty aria-label is a label this test judges, with working fixtures where the aria-label is the one effective source and where another source takes precedence. The only exception is the glossary's order of the accessible name, which puts aria-labelledby before aria-label; the check abstains on fields with aria-labelledby, and also on fields with a <label>, title or placeholder, since the order does not say whether an empty aria-label gives way to them. The glossary's note that aria-label cannot be used to indicate that a field is required is not a condition of this test's wording, and nothing is claimed from it. No axe rule is tagged for this test. Applicability is judgment: whether a field's label is provided by its aria-label turns on the order of the accessible name and on whether an empty attribute counts, which the text leaves open. Needs is empty.

citations.quote: Chaque étiquette associée à un champ de formulaire est-elle pertinente (hors cas particuliers) ?
Le champ de formulaire possède un attribut WAI-ARIA `aria-label` ;
Note : l’attribut aria-label ne peut pas être utilisé pour indiquer le caractère obligatoire d’un champ.
Si c’est le cas pour chaque champ de formulaire, **le test est validé**.
